questions.question: In a class of 100 students, every student has passed in one or more of the three subjects, i.e History, Economics and English. Among all the student, 24 students have passed in English only, 14 students have passed in History only 11 students have passed in both English and Economics only, and 12 students have passed in both English and History only. A total of 50 students have passed in History. If only 5 students have passed in all three subjects, then how many students have passed in Economies only?
questions.questionHtml: In a class of 100 students, every student has passed in one or more of the three subjects, i.e History, Economics and English. Among all the student, 24 students have passed in English only, 14 students have passed in History only 11 students have passed in both English and Economics only, and 12 students have passed in both English and History only. A total of 50 students have passed in History. If only 5 students have passed in all three subjects, then how many students have passed in Economies only?
questions.solution:
Total no. of students in the class = 100

No. of students passed in English only = 24

No. of students passed in History only = 14

No. of students passed in both English and Economics only = 11

No. of students passed in both English and History only = 12

No. of students passed in History = 50

No. of students passed in all three subjects = 5

No. of students who passed in Economics only = 100 - (50 + 24 + 11) = 100 - 85 = 15.

Hence, 15 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which two signs and two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 28 – 32 ÷ 2 × 8 + 34 = 132
questions.questionHtml:
Which two signs and two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

28 – 32 ÷ 2 × 8 + 34 = 132
questions.solution:
Given equation: 28 – 32 ÷ 2 × 8 + 34 = 132

1) × and -; 32 and 34

Interchanging according to the option

 28 × 34 ÷ 2 – 8 + 32

= 28 × 17 – 8 + 32

= 476 – 8 + 32

= 508 – 8

= 500 ≠ 132

2) + AND -; 32 and 34

Interchanging according to the option

28 + 34 ÷ 2 × 8 – 32

= 28 + 17 × 8 – 32

= 28 + 136 – 32

= 164 – 32

= 132

3) + and -; 28 and 32

Interchanging according to the option

32 + 28 ÷ 2 × 8 – 34

= 32 + 14 × 8 – 34

= 32 + 112 – 34

= 144 – 34

= 110 ≠ 132

4) × and -; 8 and 2

Interchanging according to the option

28 × 32 ÷ 8 – 2 + 34

= 28 × 4 – 2 + 34

= 112 – 2 + 34

= 146 – 2

= 144 ≠ 132

Hence, + AND -; 32 and 34 is the correct answer.

questions.question: The distance between two stations, A and B, is 428 km. a train starts from station ‘A’ at 6:00 a.m and moves towards station ‘B’ at an average speed of 48 km/h. Another train starts from station ‘B’ at 6:20 a.m and moves towards statin ‘A’ at an average speed of 55 km/h. At what time will the trains meet?
questions.questionHtml: The distance between two stations, A and B, is 428 km. a train starts from station ‘A’ at 6:00 a.m and moves towards station ‘B’ at an average speed of 48 km/h. Another train starts from station ‘B’ at 6:20 a.m and moves towards statin ‘A’ at an average speed of 55 km/h. At what time will the trains meet?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Train A travels alone for 20 minutes (1/3 hour) → Distance = 48 × (1/3) = 16 km.

Remaining distance at 6:20 a.m. = 428 − 16 = 412 km.

Relative speed = 48 + 55 = 103 km/h.

Time to meet = 412 ÷ 103 = 4 hours after 6:20 a.m.

∴ The correct answer is 10:20 a.m.

Alternate Method

Given: Total Distance = 428 km, Speed of Train A = 48 km/h (starts 6:00 a.m.), Speed of Train B = 55 km/h (starts 6:20 a.m.).

Formula Used: Distance = Speed × Time; Relative Speed (Opposite direction) = S1 + S2.

⇒ Distance covered by Train A in 20 mins = 48 × (20/60) = 16 km.

⇒ Distance between trains at 6:20 a.m. = 428 − 16 = 412 km.

⇒ Relative speed = 48 + 55 = 103 km/h.

⇒ Time taken to meet = 412 ÷ 103 = 4 hours.

⇒ Meeting time = 6:20 a.m. + 4 hours = 10:20 a.m.

∴ The correct answer is 10:20 a.m.

Additional Information

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move toward each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Srel = S1 + S2.

Meeting Time Rule

To calculate meeting time, ensure both objects start moving from their respective positions at the same reference time by calculating initial distance covered.

Unit Conversion

Always convert time into hours when speed is in km/h: 1 minute = 1/60 hour.
